added.summary: A timeline has a `scene` track: `track scene { key 0 { scene "scenes/kitchen.ogt" } }`. From a key to the next (or `scene none`) that scene is in the world, its entities under a root that is a child of the og.Timeline's entity, so a cutscene, a level or a minigame brings its own world and takes it away. The cut happens between ticks: the tick whose time reaches the key decides and the next starts with the old scene gone and the new one in place, on every host, in a replay and after a restore. A timeline that ends keeps its scene until it is stopped; a seek inside a key keeps the scene that is there. The cook refuses a scene the bundle lacks, and a timeline now needs the engine modules of the scenes, videos and timelines its tracks name.

og.scene.progress says whether the scene would be drawn whole the frame it is placed: every streaming group in, and everything it spawns with loaded, with no pipeline of it still compiling. Wait for it instead of `ready` to change scene without a first-frame hitch.

fixed.summary: Preloading a scene now also loads what it spawns with, without placing it: its models and their textures into the renderer, their pipelines started, its sub-scenes and prefabs. That work moves from the tick of og.scene.change to the preload call. A timeline in pre-roll or playing prepares the scenes its scene tracks name the same way, and a display frame holds the clock while a scene a timeline cuts to is still being read or prepared (the page is told it is buffering, as for og.VideoPlayer.wait). A game that counted on og.scene.preload returning before a scene's models were decoded should call it earlier, such as when the previous level starts.
